summary: 1928 Fisher Forestry lookout at Number Four, Lewis County, NY; closed in the early 1980s, and its upper section now stands at the DEC Lowville demonstration area.

facts.design: Aermotor LX25 steel tower with ladders between landings at first, later stairs; glass-enclosed observatory
facts.status_note: Only the upper section stands, at the DEC Lowville demonstration area; the original Number Four site keeps only the tower footers
facts.agency: NYS Department of Environmental Conservation (Lowville demonstration area)

access.note: DEC demonstration area in Lowville; the DEC invites visitors to climb to the observation cabin at the top

visit.trail_note: On the DEC Lowville demonstration area; the DEC office sits just past the tower

events.note: Erected by the Fisher Forestry and Realty Company with Conservation Department co-operation. Sources give 75, 80 and 90 feet for the height.
Conservation Department took over operation from the landowner; the duties of the Beaver Lake Mountain lookout were transferred to Number Four
Observer's cabin and standard stairs added, replacing the ladders (per a 2019 post by Fred Knauf). Wikipedia dates the stair change to about 1960.
Land holding with the cabin and tower transferred from the landowner to the state (Wikipedia)
Ladders replaced with stairs, around 1960 (Wikipedia; conflicts with the 1945 date in the newsletter)
Final year of operation, the operations discontinued (eastern lookouts record); Wikipedia says closed in the early 1980s
Observer's cabin moved to Nicks Lake Campground around 1984 (Wikipedia)
Tower removed from the original site; the chief reason cited was extensive vandalism

evidence.supports: Fisher Forestry and Realty Company erected a steel tower at Number Four with Conservation Department co-operation in 1928
evidence.quote: The Fisher Forestry and Realty Company has recently completed, with the co-operation of the Conservation Department the erection of a steel fire tower near Number Four.

evidence.supports: newspapers describe the tower as nearly 80 feet high with an observatory enclosed in glass
evidence.quote: The tower is nearly 80 feet in height and of modern type, having observatory enclosed with glass.

evidence.supports: a 2018 reader quoted in the newsletter says the tower was originally 75 feet
evidence.quote: tower was originally 75' tall, now it has been shortened to 25' and stands at the DEC demonstration area

evidence.supports: the DEC says the original tower was 90 feet tall
evidence.quote: The original tower was 90 feet tall and used to detect fire in the surrounding landscape.

evidence.supports: Wikipedia describes a 75-foot Aermotor LX25 tower built in 1928 with ladders rather than stairs
evidence.quote: In 1928, the Fisher Forestry Company with supervision from the Conservation Department built a 75-foot-tall (23 m) Aermotor Corporation LX25 tower, with ladders rather than stairs between the landings.

evidence.supports: the landowner ran the tower until 1945, when the Conservation Department took over operation
evidence.quote: The tower was owned and operated by the landowner until 1945 when the Conservation Department took over operation.

evidence.supports: the duties of the Beaver Lake Mountain lookout moved to Number Four in 1945
evidence.quote: 1945: The duties of the Beaver Lake Mountain Lookout were transferred to the Number 4 lookout.

evidence.supports: Knauf says an observer's cabin and standard stairs were added in 1945, replacing the ladders
evidence.quote: An observer’s cabin and the normal style stairs were added in 1945 which replaced the ladder style stairs.

evidence.supports: the 1945 account is a 2019 Facebook post by Fred Knauf
evidence.quote: In 2019 Fred Knauf noted the following on Facebook

evidence.supports: Wikipedia says the ladders were replaced with stairs around 1960
evidence.quote: Around 1960, the ladders were all replaced with stairs.

evidence.supports: the land passed from the landowner to the state in 1958
evidence.quote: In 1958, the piece of land that included the cabin and tower, was transferred from landowner to the state of New York.

evidence.supports: 1982 was the final year, when operations were discontinued
evidence.quote: 1982: The final year, the operations discontinued.

evidence.supports: Wikipedia says the tower closed in the early 1980s and was later dismantled and removed
evidence.quote: The tower was closed in the early 1980s, and was later dismantled and removed.

evidence.supports: the tower was removed, with extensive vandalism the chief reason cited
evidence.quote: 1987: The tower removed, the chief reason cited was the extensive vandalism.

evidence.supports: the DEC says the upper section was moved to and displayed near the Demonstration Area entrance
evidence.quote: The upper section of the tower was moved to and displayed near the entrance of the Demonstration Area.

evidence.supports: Wikipedia says the upper section was used to build a demonstration tower beside the DEC office at Lowville
evidence.quote: The upper section of the tower was used to build the demonstration tower adjacent to the Lowville Department of Environmental Conservation office.

evidence.supports: the observer's cabin was moved to Nicks Lake Campground around 1984
evidence.quote: Around 1984 the observer cabin was moved to Nicks Lake Campground.

evidence.supports: the ranger cabin at Lowville was moved from Gomer Hill
evidence.quote: A Ranger cabin sits at the base of the fire tower. It was moved to the Demonstration Area from Gomer Hill.

evidence.supports: the DEC says visitors should feel free to climb to the observation cabin at the top
evidence.quote: Visitors should feel free to climb the tower to the observation cabin at the top.

evidence.supports: the DEC office sits just past the fire tower
evidence.quote: Continue 1.3 miles to office on left, just past fire tower.

evidence.supports: only the tower footers remain at the former site
evidence.quote: Nothing remains at the former tower site except for the tower footers.

evidence.supports: the FFLA New York list gives the Lowville tower as the relocated Number Four
evidence.quote: Lowville Demonstration Forest (Relocated Number Four)

evidence.supports: a 2018 reader spells the builder Fischer and dates the state turnover to about 1945
evidence.quote: It was built by the Fischer Forestry & Reality Co. and turned over to the state around 1945.

corrections.current: Number Four Fire Tower (now at Lowville Demonstration Forest)
corrections.proposed: Number Four Fire Tower (upper section now at Lowville Demonstration Area)
corrections.why: The DEC page describes the upper section as moved and displayed at its Demonstration Area; the record's wording suggests the whole tower moved

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 2018 reader's quote in the newsletter spells the company Fischer; the 1928 newspapers and the 2019 post spell it Fisher, so both name the same firm

sources.title: Forest Fire Lookout Association, New York State Chapter newsletter, June 2023
sources.publisher: Forest Fire Lookout Association, New York State Chapter

notes_for_editor: Height is disputed (75 ft in a 2018 reader quote and Wikipedia, about 80 ft in 1928 newspapers, 90 ft on the DEC page), so no height_m is set. Stair change conflicts: 1945 per Knauf via the 2023 newsletter, about 1960 per Wikipedia. The Aermotor LX25 model and the 1958 land transfer rest on Wikipedia alone. Date of the upper section's move to Lowville not found, so no relocated event with a year. The DEC page gives no opening hours; access uses the DEC invitation to climb. Andy Arthur's page returned HTTP 403 and was not read. Facebook search snippets (Tug Hill Commission, FFLA NYS group) were seen only as search results and are not cited. Reads used: 6 (newsletter PDF, Andy Arthur 403, cached eastern page, cached FFLA NY list, DEC page, Wikipedia); one fallback web search.
